commentary_title: Strong long-haul product flows continue to support LR2 earnings
commentary_summary: LR2 utilisation remained firm at 91.9% in Week 45, while the tonne-mile index reached 142.9, up 19.5% YoY, reflecting continued strength in long-haul clean product trade. The combination of rising tonne-mile demand and elevated utilisation suggests that cargo growth is continuing to absorb available fleet capacity despite the gradual increase in fleet productivity. | Vessel availability tightened further during the month as global tonnage at anchor declined by 1.5 mdwt on a four-week moving average basis, while anchored capacity fell by 10.0% MoM in the West and 1.0% MoM in the East. The share of laden vessels increased by 1.5 percentage points in the West, indicating stronger cargo employment and a tighter supply-demand balance in Atlantic markets. | Market conditions remained constructive despite bunker prices remaining elevated at USD 990/tonne. Spot earnings strengthened across both TC1 and TC8 routes as lower idle capacity and robust cargo demand outweighed productivity gains. Congestion also remained elevated in the Atlantic and Indian Ocean regions, helping absorb vessel availability.
